1 km = ? cm

1 km = 100 000 cm

Learn these first. Every map and plan question uses them!

🏠 Menu

🛏️ The tiny bed

Plan scale 1 cm : 50 cm. The bed is 4 cm on the plan. Jay orders a 4 cm bed online.

How long should the bed really be?

🤔 Guess first! Write it down.

Step 1

1 cm on the plan = 50 cm real

× 50

Step 2

4 × 50 cm (1 m = 100 cm)

200 cm = 2 m

2 m. A 4 cm bed is for a hamster! 🛏️

Scale drawings: EASY

Q1

No calculator

[2 marks]

Alan makes a model of a steam train. The scale he uses is 1 cm represents 60 cm. (a) A wheel on the model is 3 cm wide. How wide is the wheel on the real train? (b) The chimney on the real train is 90 cm tall. How tall is the chimney on the model?

Hint

Answer

Model to real: ×. Real to model: divide.

Answer: (a) 180 cm (b) 1.5 cm

solve →

Q2

No calculator

[2 marks]

A model of a house is made using the scale 1 : 30. A door on the model is 7 cm high. What is the height of the door on the real house? Give your answer in metres.

Hint

Answer

× 30, then divide by 100. (1 m = 100 cm)

Answer: 2.1 m

solve →

Q3

No calculator

[2 marks]

Robin has a scale drawing of his local park. The scale is 1 cm represents 250 cm. The real bandstand is 10 m wide. How wide is the bandstand on the drawing?

Hint

Answer

Change m to cm first. (1 m = 100 cm)

Answer: 4 cm

solve →

Hard 1: mixed

Q1

Calculator

[5 marks]

A floor plan has a scale of 1 : 50. A room measures 9 cm by 7 cm on the plan. Carpet costs £18 per square metre. Mia has £280 to spend on carpet for the room. Is this enough?

Hint

Answer

Find real lengths in metres first. (1 m = 100 cm)

Answer: No: £283.50 > £280

solve →

Q2

Calculator

[5 marks]

A map has a scale of 1 cm to 2.5 km. A ferry route measures 6.4 cm on the map. The ferry travels at 20 km/h. It leaves at 09:40. At what time does it arrive? The ferry must arrive by 10:30 to meet a train. Does it?

Hint

Answer

Distance first, then the time. (1 hour = 60 minutes)

Answer: 10:28: yes, in time

solve →

Q3

Calculator

[5 marks]

A map has a scale of 1 : 25 000. A rectangular field measures 6.4 cm by 4.5 cm on the map. A farmer needs a field of at least 150 hectares. 1 square kilometre = 100 hectares. Is the field big enough?

Hint

Answer

Real lengths in km first, then the area. (1 km = 100 000 cm)

Answer: Yes: 180 hectares

solve →
